newsitem.title: JAPAN: RUBBER-Japan market seen falling, eyes spot expiry.
newsitem.headline: RUBBER-Japan market seen falling, eyes spot expiry.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures are likely to fall further next week, as book squaring ahead of the spot July contract expiry on July 25 is expected to cap the topside, Japanese traders said on Friday.
Traders said that the benchmark December 1997 contract is expected to fall at least to 110 yen next week.

"Book squaring in the spot month will be a key factor for the rubber market next week. I expect volatile price movements until next Friday," a rubber analyst at a Tokyo-based commodity brokerage house said.
There were 4,648 lots of open interest in spot July on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) as of July 16.
Benchmark December rubber futures on TOCOM ended the morning session at 114.1 yen per kg on Friday, against Thursday's close of 114.4 yen.
Benchmark December rubber on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 114.4 yen, compared with 113.7 yen on Thursday.
Local traders said they are watching to see if the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) enters the market to support prices.

An INRO official said last Friday the group could enter the market "anytime" to support rubber prices if they stay at the current rate or slip to the "must buy" level of 172 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg.
"We haven't seen any actual buying by the INRO this week, but we will keep watching their actions next week," a trader at another commodity brokerage house said.
Thai rubber offer prices to Japan were at 95.00 U.S. cents per kg on an FOB basis on Friday, against 90.00 U.S. cents on July 11.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 120.0 yen per kg as of Friday, against 119.0 yen a week ago.
